Action hooks::useActionState.summary: useActionState connects a form action to its latest returned state and pending status. It returns a wrapped action for forms or buttons, making async submission results easy to render.
Action hooks::useActionState.explanation: Call useActionState at the top level with an action and initial state. React supplies the previous state to the action, returns the action's latest result, and exposes a wrapped action for a form plus a pending flag.
Action hooks::useActionState.syntax: const [state, formAction, isPending] = useActionState(fn, initialState, permalink?);

parameters.name: fn
parameters.description: The function called on form submission or button activation. It receives previous state first, followed by the usual form-action arguments.

parameters.name: initialState
parameters.description: The initial state value. It may be any serializable value and is ignored after the action is first invoked.

parameters.name: permalink
parameters.description: Optional URL used for progressive enhancement when the form is submitted before hydration.

Action hooks::useActionState.returns: An array containing the current state, a wrapped form action, and an isPending flag.

example.title: Display form action state
example.explanation: The action receives the previous state and submitted FormData, while the component renders the latest result and pending status.

useCases.title: Form validation
useCases.scenario: Show validation errors returned by an async form action.

useCases.title: Pending feedback
useCases.scenario: Disable inputs and display progress during submission.

useCases.title: Action result UI
useCases.scenario: Render the latest response from a server or client action.

keyPoints: Use it when a form action should produce state that the component can render.
The action receives the previous state as its first argument, enabling stateful validation or result handling.
After submission, state represents the action's most recent returned value.
Use the returned formAction as the form's action or as a button's formAction.
Use isPending to disable controls or show progress while the action is running.
gotchas: It is a Hook, so call it only at the top level of a component or custom Hook; do not put it in loops or conditions.
The initialState value is used only before the first invocation; later renders use the action's previous return value.
Choose an initial state that can be serialized, especially when the action is used with server-rendered forms.

Action hooks::useActionState server acti.summary: useActionState wraps a form or server action and exposes its latest returned state plus pending status. Return structured validation data from the server action to render field-specific errors in the form.
Action hooks::useActionState server acti.explanation: Pass a server function and an initial result to useActionState, then attach the returned action to a form. The function receives the previous state before the submitted form data, and its returned value becomes the next state, allowing field errors and success data to render. The hook also supplies pending status and can support progressive enhancement with a permalink.
Action hooks::useActionState server acti.syntax: const [state, dispatchAction, isPending] = useActionState(reducerAction, initialState, permalink?);

parameters.name: reducerAction
parameters.description: The function called when the Action runs; it receives previous state first and the action payload second.

parameters.name: initialState
parameters.description: The state used during the first render.

parameters.name: permalink
parameters.description: Optional unique URL for the form's modified page, used for progressive enhancement.

Action hooks::useActionState server acti.returns: A three-item array: the current state, a dispatchAction function, and a boolean isPending indicating whether the Action is pending.

example.title: Server-backed form validation
example.explanation: The wrapped action validates the submitted email and returns structured errors or a success message, which the component renders.

useCases.title: Server-side field validation
useCases.scenario: Validate submitted fields on the server and return an object containing field-to-message mappings.

useCases.title: Render action results
useCases.scenario: Display the latest server response, such as a success message or a rejected submission.

useCases.title: Pending form state
useCases.scenario: Disable controls while the submitted Action is running.

useCases.title: Progressive enhancement
useCases.scenario: Support submissions before client JavaScript loads on dynamic Server Component pages.

keyPoints: It stores the latest value returned by an Action and exposes that value to the component.
Use the hook at component top level rather than inside conditions, loops, or nested functions.
The action receives previous state first, followed by the payload supplied by the returned dispatcher.
The second tuple item is the wrapped action to provide to a form or invoke within an Action.
The first tuple item starts as the initial state and changes to the action's latest returned result.
The optional permalink supports form submissions before JavaScript loads on compatible Server Component pages.
gotchas: Call the returned action through a form action or another Action; invoking it as an ordinary event callback does not satisfy this requirement.
Showing the response before hydration requires a framework and setup that support React Server Components and Server Functions.
Use the optional permalink for dynamic pages so a pre-hydration submission navigates to the intended page.

Action hooks::useFormStatus.summary: useFormStatus lets a component rendered inside a form read the latest submission status of its parent form. Use its pending value to update nested submit controls while submission is active.
Action hooks::useFormStatus.explanation: Call useFormStatus from a component rendered inside the form. It reads the nearest parent form's latest submission status, including whether submission is pending and, when available, the submitted data, method, and action function.
Action hooks::useFormStatus.syntax: const { pending, data, method, action } = useFormStatus();
Action hooks::useFormStatus.returns: An object with pending, data, method, and action properties. pending is boolean; data is FormData or null; method is 'get' or 'post'; action is the parent form's action function or null.

example.title: Disable a nested submit button while submitting
example.explanation: The nested submit button disables itself and changes its label while its parent form action is pending.

useCases.title: Pending submit control
useCases.scenario: Disable a submit button and change its label while the parent form is submitting.

useCases.title: Submission details
useCases.scenario: Inspect the FormData currently being submitted to display contextual feedback.

useCases.title: Method-aware form UI
useCases.scenario: Adapt nested UI to whether the parent form uses GET or POST.

keyPoints: It lets nested controls observe the latest submission state of their parent form.
Use it for submission-aware UI such as disabling a submit button or showing progress text.
Read pending to determine whether the parent form is currently submitting.
The return value is a status object containing pending, data, method, and action.
data exposes the current submission's FormData, or null when no submission is active or no parent form exists.
method identifies whether the parent form submits with GET or POST.
action refers to the parent form's function action; it is null when the form has no applicable function action.
gotchas: Calling the Hook in the same component that returns the form does not read that form's status; put it in a nested component.
The Hook reports only a parent form's status, not a form rendered by the component itself or by a descendant.

Action hooks::useOptimistic.summary: useOptimistic lets a component display an expected state while an Action is awaiting its real result. React uses the confirmed value again after the Action completes or fails.
Action hooks::useOptimistic.explanation: Call the Hook at component top level with the confirmed value and optionally a pure reducer. It returns the value to render plus a setter; calling that setter inside an Action temporarily applies the optimistic value, then React returns to the confirmed value when the Action finishes or fails.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The confirmed value used when no Action is pending.

parameters.name: reducer
parameters.description: Optional pure function receiving current state and an action, returning the next optimistic state.

parameters.name: optimisticState
parameters.description: The temporary value to display during an Action; with a reducer, it becomes the reducer's action argument.

Action hooks::useOptimistic.returns: An array containing the current optimistic state and a setter that temporarily changes it during an Action.

example.title: Optimistic like count
example.explanation: The button runs an Action that immediately displays the incremented count while the save request is pending.

useCases.title: Instant mutation feedback
useCases.scenario: Show a changed count, label, or status immediately while a server mutation is pending.

useCases.title: Responsive form submission
useCases.scenario: Render a submitted item with a temporary pending indicator before the server confirms it.

useCases.title: Reducer-based collection updates
useCases.scenario: Apply an optimistic list insertion, deletion, or update using an action payload.

keyPoints: Use it to show an expected result immediately while an asynchronous Action is still running.
The Hook accepts a confirmed value and an optional reducer, returning state and an optimistic setter.
Declare it at the component's top level, not inside conditions, loops, or nested functions.
The first argument is the authoritative value shown when no Action is pending.
A reducer computes the temporary state from the current state and the action payload.
Destructure the result into the currently rendered optimistic state and its setter.
An in-Action setter call re-renders immediately with the temporary state.
Outside a pending Action, rendering falls back to the confirmed input value.
gotchas: Calling the setter outside an Action warns and only briefly renders the optimistic state.
Do not invoke the optimistic setter during ordinary event handling unless that handler starts an Action.
Keep the reducer pure and return the next optimistic state from its current state and action.

Action hooks::useOptimistic rollback.summary: When an optimistic Action fails, React renders the unchanged source value, making the UI automatically return to its pre-update state. The optimistic setter must run inside an Action.
Action hooks::useOptimistic rollback.explanation: useOptimistic overlays a temporary result while an Action is running. If the Action fails, React ends the Transition and renders the current source value; because that value normally changes only after success, the UI automatically returns to its pre-update state.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The current, non-optimistic value used as the source of truth after the Action finishes.

parameters.name: updateFn
parameters.description: A function that receives the current state and the optimistic action argument, returning the temporary state.

Action hooks::useOptimistic rollback.returns: An array containing the current optimistic state and a setter that schedules an optimistic update.

example.title: Automatic rollback after a failed Action
example.explanation: The optimistic item disappears during the Action; when the request fails and the source state remains unchanged, React renders the item again.

useCases.title: Optimistic deletion
useCases.scenario: Remove an item immediately while a delete request runs, then show it again if deletion fails.

useCases.title: Optimistic editing
useCases.scenario: Display an edited label before the server confirms the update, reverting when the update fails.

useCases.title: Fast feedback for mutations
useCases.scenario: Show a pending reaction or vote instantly while the mutation is submitted.

keyPoints: The optimistic value is displayed only while its Action is pending.
Outside an active Action, the hook returns the source value rather than the temporary optimistic result.
Rollback is driven by the current source value supplied as the hook’s first argument.
If the server mutation fails and the parent leaves the source state unchanged, the previous UI reappears automatically.
React converges the optimistic and real state without requiring a separate reset render.
gotchas: Call the optimistic setter inside an Action; otherwise React warns and the optimistic state only appears briefly before reverting.
A failed Action does not restore an old snapshot independently; rollback comes from rendering the current `value`, so keep that source of truth unchanged on failure.
Automatic rollback does not provide user-facing error feedback; catch the failure when the interface should explain what happened.

Async hooks::use.summary: Read a Promise or context value during rendering with use. Promises integrate with Suspense: pending reads suspend, and the resolved value is returned when ready.
Async hooks::use.explanation: use reads a Promise or context during rendering. For a Promise, React suspends the component while it is pending and resumes it with the resolved value; a surrounding Suspense boundary displays a fallback during that wait.

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description: A Promise whose resolved value you want to read, or a context whose value you want to read.

Async hooks::use.returns: The resource's value: the resolved Promise value or the context value.

example.title: Read a Promise with use
example.explanation: The component reads a cached Promise with use; it suspends until the Promise resolves, while Suspense renders the fallback.

useCases.title: Suspense-enabled data reading
useCases.scenario: Read data supplied as a cached Promise and show loading UI with Suspense.

useCases.title: Asynchronous context values
useCases.scenario: Share a Promise through context without passing it through every component.

useCases.title: Conditional context access
useCases.scenario: Read context conditionally or inside a loop where useContext cannot be called.

keyPoints: use reads a Promise or context resource during render.
Passing a context returns its current context value.
Passing a Promise returns its resolved value once available.
A pending Promise suspends the component that called use.
Suspense shows its fallback while the Promise remains pending.
A rejected Promise is handled by the nearest Error Boundary.
gotchas: Pass a cached Promise rather than creating a new Promise during rendering; React needs the same instance across re-renders.
Conditional and loop calls are allowed, but the Promise itself must always be passed to use.
Do not inspect Promise internals to avoid suspension; pass the Promise to use.

Async hooks::use with conditional contex.summary: Use reads a context value during rendering and may be called conditionally or inside loops. This makes it suitable when useContext's top-level-only rule would prevent a context read.
Async hooks::use with conditional contex.explanation: Use the React use API with a context object to read its current value during rendering. Unlike useContext, use may appear after an early return or inside a conditional or loop, but the calling function must still be a component or Hook. React applies the nearest provider's value, or the context default when no provider exists.

parameters.name: resource
parameters.type: resource, such as a Promise or context
parameters.description: A context object created with createContext; use reads the context value available to the calling component.

Async hooks::use with conditional contex.returns: The value of the supplied resource; for a context, this is the current context value.

example.title: Conditional context read
example.explanation: Reads the context only when the condition is true, which is allowed for use but not for useContext.

useCases.title: Read context after an early return
useCases.scenario: A component returns early unless a prop or child is present, then needs context.

useCases.title: Conditional styling or rendering
useCases.scenario: A context is needed only for one conditional rendering branch.

useCases.title: Context access in a loop
useCases.scenario: A component needs context while iterating over conditionally processed items.

keyPoints: Pass a context object to use to obtain that context's value during render.
use supports context reads inside conditionals and loops, unlike useContext's top-level restriction.
For context, use follows the same provider-based reading behavior as useContext.
The function calling use must be a React component or a custom Hook.
use is a React API rather than a Hook, so the standard top-level Hook call restriction does not apply to it.
gotchas: Do not bypass use for Promise resources by reading their internal status or value directly; pass the Promise to use.

Async hooks::use with promises.summary: Read a stable Promise during rendering with use. React suspends while it is pending, renders the resolved value afterward, and sends rejections to the nearest Error Boundary.
Async hooks::use with promises.explanation: Pass a cached Promise to use during component rendering. React suspends the component while the Promise is pending, returns its resolved value after completion, and sends a rejection to the nearest Error Boundary.

parameters.name: promise
parameters.description: A Promise whose resolved value you want to read. The Promise must be cached so that the same instance is reused across re-renders.

Async hooks::use with promises.returns: The value read from the resource, such as the resolved value of the Promise.

example.title: Read a promise with use
example.explanation: Reads a cached promise during rendering, showing Suspense content while it is pending.

useCases.title: Render async data
useCases.scenario: A component receives a cached data Promise from a Suspense-enabled framework.

useCases.title: Read streamed server data
useCases.scenario: A Client Component needs to consume a Promise passed from a Server Component.

useCases.title: Suspend with a fallback
useCases.scenario: A component needs loading UI while resource data is pending.

keyPoints: use reads a Promise resource while the component renders.
Pending work suspends the component until the Promise settles.
Wrap the reading component in Suspense to provide loading UI.
gotchas: Do not create a new Promise during each render; reuse a cached Promise instance.
A rejected Promise is handled by an Error Boundary, not by a returned error value.
Although use may be conditional or inside a loop, do not skip the call merely because the Promise may already be settled.

Concurrency hooks::useDeferredValue.summary: useDeferredValue lets a slower part of the UI lag behind an urgent value. React keeps urgent updates responsive, then renders the deferred value in the background.
Concurrency hooks::useDeferredValue.explanation: Call the Hook at the top level with a value whose updates should be deprioritized. React returns the previous value first during an update, then attempts a background render with the new value; the background work can catch up without holding up more urgent UI. An optional initial value can replace the value only for the first render.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The value whose update should be deferred; it may have any type.

parameters.name: initialValue
parameters.description: Optional value returned during the initial render. Without it, the current value is returned initially.

Concurrency hooks::useDeferredValue.returns: The deferred value: initialValue or value on the first render, the previous value during the initial update render, and eventually the new value after the background render.

example.title: Keep search results behind the input
example.explanation: The input responds immediately while the results receive the deferred query and may temporarily display the previous value.

useCases.title: Responsive search
useCases.scenario: A text field updates immediately while a costly filtered list catches up.

useCases.title: Stale content during loading
useCases.scenario: A Suspense-backed result view should keep showing previous results while new data loads.

useCases.title: Defer expensive rendering
useCases.scenario: A non-critical visualization or large list should not block urgent controls.

keyPoints: Call it at component top level and use the returned value for the slower UI path.
The urgent render can keep the previous deferred value while React starts the update with the latest value in the background.
React later retries the slower path using the new value when rendering capacity is available.
The input may be any type, although stable primitives or objects created outside rendering are the practical choice.
Pass initialValue when the first render should use a placeholder rather than the current value.

Concurrency hooks::useDeferredValue init.summary: useDeferredValue(value, initialValue?) lets a component show a chosen fallback on its initial render, then defer rendering the supplied value. It is useful for starting a loading or filtered view with an intentionally simple value.
Concurrency hooks::useDeferredValue init.explanation: Pass an optional second argument to useDeferredValue when the initial render should use a deliberate fallback instead of the current value. React uses that fallback initially and later renders the supplied value in the background.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The value to defer; it can have any type.

parameters.name: initialValue
parameters.description: Optional value used during the component’s initial render. If omitted, the initial render is not deferred.

Concurrency hooks::useDeferredValue init.returns: currentValue: the initialValue during the initial render when supplied, otherwise value; during updates, the previous value may be returned first and the new value is attempted in the background.

example.title: Defer an initially empty filtered view
example.explanation: Uses an empty query for the initial render, then lets React update the filtered view with the current query in the background.

useCases.title: Initial empty filtered view
useCases.scenario: A search or filter view should begin with no filter, then populate from the current query.

useCases.title: Initial loading view
useCases.scenario: A costly results component should show a lightweight initial state before rendering current data.

useCases.title: Defer secondary content
useCases.scenario: A non-critical UI section should update after more urgent content has rendered.

keyPoints: Call the Hook at the component’s top level and use its result wherever the non-critical UI should lag.
The deferred source and initial value are not restricted to strings; they can represent any value type.
With initialValue, the first render receives that fallback; without it, the first render receives value.
On later updates, React first renders with the previous deferred value before attempting the newer one.
React schedules a background render that eventually applies the current value.
gotchas: Without initialValue, the initial render is not deferred because React has no earlier value to display.
The deferred result can temporarily lag behind the current value during updates.
Do not assume the deferred value updates synchronously with the source value.

Concurrency hooks::useTransition pending.summary: useTransition provides isPending for feedback while a Transition is active and startTransition for marking non-urgent updates. Use the flag to disable duplicate interactions or show progress.
Concurrency hooks::useTransition pending.explanation: Call the Hook in a component, then wrap non-urgent state updates in its startTransition function. React sets isPending to true while the Transition is processing and keeps it true until the Actions finish and the final state is displayed, allowing feedback or duplicate-interaction prevention.

example.title: Show pending feedback for a tab transition
example.explanation: Use the returned boolean to disable tab buttons and display feedback while the transition is active.

useCases.title: Prevent duplicate navigation
useCases.scenario: Disable navigation or tab controls while a Transition is pending.

useCases.title: Show progress feedback
useCases.scenario: Render a spinner or loading message during an in-progress Transition.

useCases.title: Preserve responsive interactions
useCases.scenario: Keep the current interface interactive while non-urgent content updates.

keyPoints: The Hook returns isPending and startTransition in a fixed two-item array.
Read isPending to determine whether a Transition is still active.
Call startTransition around non-urgent state updates so React can process them as a Transition.
Pending feedback begins when the first startTransition call starts the Transition.
The pending flag remains true until all Actions finish and React displays the final state.
Use the boolean for a spinner, loading message, disabled control, or another in-progress visual state.
gotchas: Keep the function passed to startTransition synchronous; for async work, updates after each await need another startTransition call.
Call useTransition only at the top level of a component or custom Hook, not from arbitrary functions.

Context hooks::use as context.summary: Read a context with use when the read must occur conditionally or inside a loop. It behaves like useContext for context lookup but permits these placements.
Context hooks::use as context.explanation: React's use API reads a context's current value during rendering. Pass the context object to use; unlike useContext, this call may appear in conditionals or loops, while still needing to run inside a component or Hook and observing use's restrictions.

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: The context object whose current value should be read.

Context hooks::use as context.returns: The current value from the nearest matching context provider above the calling component.

example.title: Conditionally read a context
example.explanation: This component reads the nearest theme context only when the rule should be rendered.

useCases.title: Conditional rendering
useCases.scenario: A component may return early before it needs context, then read it only for the rendered branch.

useCases.title: Loop-based reads
useCases.scenario: A component processes multiple context-dependent items or resources in a loop.

useCases.title: Flexible context access
useCases.scenario: A component needs ordinary context semantics but more flexible call placement than useContext provides.

keyPoints: use reads a resource during render; for this card, the resource is a context.
Pass the context object directly to use to obtain its current value.
Use is useful when context access must happen conditionally or while iterating.
Context lookup and reading behave like useContext, but the call placement is more flexible.
The returned value comes from the nearest matching provider above the component.
gotchas: Do not bypass use for Promises by reading their status or value directly; pass the Promise to use instead.
A provider returned by the component itself does not affect a use call in that same component; the provider must be above it.

Effect hooks::Hook dependency arrays.summary: An Effect dependency array lists every reactive value read by the Effect’s setup code. React re-runs the Effect after the initial commit and when any listed dependency changes.
Effect hooks::Hook dependency arrays.explanation: An Effect’s dependency array lists every reactive value its setup code reads, including props, state, and variables or functions declared in the component. React compares the dependencies between commits and re-runs the Effect after the initial commit and when a dependency changes. Keep the list inline with a constant number of items; use [] only when the code reads no reactive values.

parameters.name: setup
parameters.description: Function that runs the synchronization logic and may return a cleanup function.

parameters.name: dependencies
parameters.description: Optional inline list of every reactive value referenced by setup; it must have a constant number of items.

example.title: Synchronize with a user ID
example.explanation: The Effect reads userId, so userId appears in the dependency array and triggers re-synchronization when it changes.

useCases.title: External synchronization
useCases.scenario: Connect to or synchronize with an external system when a prop or state value changes.

useCases.title: Data synchronization
useCases.scenario: Re-fetch or update displayed data when an identifier changes.

useCases.title: Non-reactive setup
useCases.scenario: Run setup once after mounting when the Effect reads no reactive values.

keyPoints: The array contains every reactive value read by the Effect’s setup function.
Props, state, and component-body variables or functions are reactive values.
With an array, the Effect runs after the initial commit and when a dependency changes.
Use an inline array with a constant length.
The code used inside the Effect determines its dependency list; it is not an arbitrary optimization choice.
gotchas: Do not construct the array dynamically or change its length; write the dependencies inline.
Do not omit a reactive value to suppress re-runs; revise the surrounding code instead.
Leaving out the array makes the Effect run after every commit.
Use [] only when the Effect reads no reactive values.

Effect hooks::useEffect.summary: useEffect synchronizes a component with an external system after it commits. React reruns the setup when dependencies change and invokes cleanup before resynchronizing or unmounting.
Effect hooks::useEffect.explanation: Call useEffect at the top level to run setup after a component commits. React reruns it when listed dependencies change, invoking the previous cleanup first; cleanup also runs when the component is removed.

parameters.name: setup
parameters.description: Function containing the Effect logic. It may optionally return a cleanup function. React runs setup after commit, reruns cleanup then setup when dependencies change, and runs cleanup on removal.

parameters.name: dependencies
parameters.description: Optional inline array with a constant number of dependencies. React compares each dependency with its previous value using Object.is.

example.title: Synchronize after rendering
example.explanation: This Effect synchronizes displayed status with the online prop and clears the pending timer before resynchronizing or unmounting.

useCases.title: Manage connections
useCases.scenario: Subscribe to or disconnect from an external service when a prop changes.

useCases.title: Manage resources
useCases.scenario: Start a timer or browser subscription and clean it up when dependencies change or the component unmounts.

useCases.title: Synchronize external widgets
useCases.scenario: Control a non-React widget or browser API after the UI has committed.

keyPoints: Use it to connect a component with something outside React, such as a browser API, widget, connection, or timer.
The setup function runs after the component commits, rather than during rendering.
When dependencies change, React cleans up the previous synchronization before starting the new one.
A returned cleanup function runs when the component unmounts, which is where subscriptions, timers, and connections should be stopped.
Declare every reactive value used by the Effect in a fixed inline dependency list.
The Hook itself has no useful return value; its behavior comes from setup and optional cleanup.
gotchas: Call useEffect only at the top level of a component or custom Hook, never inside loops or conditions.
Avoid Effects for ordinary calculations or state transformations that do not synchronize with an external system.
Write a fixed-length dependency array inline; do not construct it dynamically.
Dependencies are compared with Object.is, so unstable object or function values can cause extra reruns.

Effect hooks::useEffect cleanup.summary: useEffect cleanup undoes work started by an Effect. React runs it before re-running the Effect when dependencies change and when the component unmounts.
Effect hooks::useEffect cleanup.explanation: A cleanup function is the optional function returned by an Effect's setup function. React runs it before setup runs again after dependency changes and when the component is removed, so it can undo subscriptions, listeners, connections, or pending work started by the Effect.

parameters.name: setup
parameters.description: Function containing the Effect setup logic; it may return a cleanup function.

parameters.name: dependencies
parameters.description: Optional list of reactive values used by the setup and cleanup functions.

Effect hooks::useEffect cleanup.returns: No return value is documented for the cleanup function itself; the setup function may return a cleanup function that React invokes during Effect resynchronization and unmount.

example.title: Disconnect a changing subscription
example.explanation: The Effect connects to the selected room and returns the matching disconnection logic. React runs cleanup before reconnecting for a changed roomId and when the component is removed.

useCases.title: Disconnect a connection
useCases.scenario: An Effect opens a chat or other external connection.

useCases.title: Unsubscribe listeners
useCases.scenario: An Effect subscribes to an external store or event source.

useCases.title: Abort or ignore fetch work
useCases.scenario: An Effect starts a request whose result may become stale.

keyPoints: Return a function from the Effect setup when the Effect starts work that must later be stopped or undone.
When dependencies change, React cleans up using the previous render's values before running setup with the new ones.
React performs the final cleanup when the component unmounts.
For external systems, pair operations such as connect/disconnect or subscribe/unsubscribe.
For fetching, cleanup should cancel the request when possible or prevent a stale response from being used.
gotchas: Cleanup is not an unmount-only hook; it runs before an Effect re-synchronizes with new dependency values.
Development may perform an extra setup-cleanup cycle after mounting, so setup and cleanup must tolerate this.
Make cleanup undo the specific work performed by setup rather than adding unrelated behavior.

Effect hooks::useEffectEvent.summary: useEffectEvent creates an Effect Event that can read the latest props and state without making its surrounding Effect reactive to those values. Call the returned function from an Effect or another Effect Event.
Effect hooks::useEffectEvent.explanation: useEffectEvent creates an Effect Event whose callback reads the latest committed props and state when called. Unlike reactive Effect code, it does not cause the surrounding Effect to re-synchronize, so it is useful for non-reactive logic triggered by an Effect.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.description: A callback containing the logic for the Effect Event; it may accept any number of arguments and return any value.

Effect hooks::useEffectEvent.returns: An Effect Event function with the same type signature as the callback.

example.explanation: The Effect reconnects only when roomId changes, while the Effect Event reads the latest theme and state-related values when invoked.

useCases.title: External connections
useCases.scenario: A connection setup should react to roomId changes but use the current theme when connected.

useCases.title: Notifications and logging
useCases.scenario: An Effect needs to log or notify using current state without restarting its synchronization.

useCases.title: Latest values in Effect logic
useCases.scenario: An Effect-triggered callback needs fresh props or state while remaining non-reactive.

keyPoints: It extracts event-like, non-reactive logic from an Effect.
